newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB - UKRAINE GRAIN, SUNSEED EXPORTS SLUMP.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - UKRAINE GRAIN, SUNSEED EXPORTS SLUMP.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE: GRAIN AND SUNSEEDS EXPORTS CONTINUE TO DECLINE
KIEV, Aug 7 - Ukrainian wheat exports totalled 540,000 tonnes in the 1996/97 crop year (July-June), down from 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
Barley exports dropped to 324,000 tonnes from 500,000 tonnes over the same period.
Ukrainian wheat exports dropped to just 16,320 tonnes in June, compared with 66,000 tonnes in the same month last year.
Barley exports declined to 9,230 tonnes from 70,000 tonnes in June 1996.
One important reason for the sharp declines in grain output is the relatively high level of domestic prices combined with a sharp decline in world prices.
Third grade wheat is being offered on domestic market at 270-300 hryvnia per tonne ($145-161), fifth grade wheat at 240-270 hryvnia ($129-145), and feed barley at 210-225 hryvnia ($113-121).
Wheat flour exports were heavily affected by a shortage in milling wheat in Ukraine, and by Russia's protective measures.
A similar situation has developed in sunseed trade -- exports have been falling rapidly since last December, when they peaked at 322,000 tonnes.
By June 1997 they had slumped to just 16,490 tonnes. Lower sunseed exports resulted from short domestic market supply.
Prices for Ukrainian sunseeds exported in June to European countries and to the U.S. averaged $202-208 f.o.b. per tonne.
Turkey was the largest buyer having contracted 9,500 tonnes at $232.6 f.o.b per tonne.
